what: Leading Gosain family of the district is that of Dharampuri (Dhatampuri in print); estate passed to the leading member of an Akhara established by Bichipuri in Maratha times; Dharampuri holds 40 villages, a Darbari, aged 66, now married with a large family
quote: 105. The leading Gosain_family in the District is that of Dhatampuri. -This family was formerly Niltang and the succession passed to the leading member of an Akhara established by Bichipuri in the time of the Marathds.

what: Akhara of the puri-named Gosains founded by Bichipuri; the Akhara has since disappeared and the succession became hereditary (married householder)
quote: The Akhara has disappeared and Dharampuri has married and has a large family to whom he is expected to leave the estate.

what: Bichipuri bore title Mahant, headed other Gosains, kept 500 Nagas (disciples) for the Raja of Nagpur and collected tribute (takoli) by force from neighbouring chiefs and zamindars
quote: Bichipuri boasted of the title of Mahant and exercised authority over other Gogains,

what: 500 Nagas kept for the Raja of Nagpur; collected takoli by force
quote: It is said that he kept a force of 500 Nagas or disciples on behalf of the Raja of Nagpur and when the neighbouring chiefs and zamindars did not pay their takoli he went and collected it by "force.

what: Bichipuri amassed a fortune, took to moneylending and acquired villages in lieu of debts (origin of the estate)
quote: He amassed a considerable fortune, took to moneylending and obtained a number of villages in lien of debts.

what: Succession of Gosain proprietors: Bichipuri, Rikhrajpuri, Bhawanpuri, Dharampuri (disciple of Bhawanpuri); -puri names (Puri order) but the text does not name the order
quote: He was succeeded by Rikhrajpuri, and Rikhrajpuri by Bbawanpuri. After the latter's death the estate passed to the present holder Dharampuri who was Bhawanpuri's disciple.

what: Gosains listed among castes holding a large number of villages in the district
quote: Brahmans, Marathas, Rajputs, Kurmis, 'Telis, Gonds, Gosains and Chamars are other castes who hold a large number of villages in this District.

what: Dharampuri Gosain named among holders of large, absentee-managed estates
quote: Such estates are held by the Kirdatts (Marathas) of Dhamtari, the Danis (Marathas) of Raipur and Dhamtari, Kapilnath, the old tahutdar of Sirpur, DharampuriGosain and the Bania family of Lawan

what: Malguzar is Dharampuri Gosain; he and his guru formerly wealthy, now impoverished by litigation
quote: The malguzar is Dharampuri Gosain. He and his guri were formerly wealthy men, but have become involved in litigation which has impoverished them considerably.

what: Malguzars are Gosains, large landowners, said to have bought the village from a Gond family in the first famine year for Rs 400
quote: The malguzars are Gosains, who are large landowners and are said to have bought the village fram a Gond family in the first famine year for Rs, 400.

what: At the Chait fair of Khalari Devi the heads of sacrificed kids go to the Gosain malguzar
quote: leaving the head (which becomes the property of the Gosain malguzar)

what: Greeting: a Gosain is greeted 'Namo Narayan' and replies 'Narayan' (Bairagi: Jai Sitaram/Sitaram)
quote: if he meets a Gosain he says, 'Namo Narayan' or 'I bow to Narayan'; and the Gosain replies, 'Narayan'.

what: Dudhadhari math/temple built by a Bairagi who lived on milk; managed by a wealthy Mahant; elaborate unfinished temple
quote: so-called because the Bairagi who built the temple lived on nothing but milk. The temple is now managed by a respectable and wealthy Mahant.

what: Bajrangdas, Mahant of Raipur (Dudhadhari), a Bairagi, owns about 30 villages mostly muafi for the temple; once held a lakh of khandis of grain
quote: Bajrangdas Mahant of Raipur is a Bairagi. He owns about 30 villages mostly muajfi for the maintenance of the Dudhadhari temple at Raipur.

what: Village held revenue-free for the Dudhadhari temple in the name of the god Ramchandra; the lambardar malguzar is a Bairagi
quote: The village is held revenuefree for the Didhadhari temple of Raipur in the name of the god Ramchandra. The lambardar malguzar is a Bairagi.

what: Village held mokasa by the Mahant of Seorinarayan for a shrine there; order not named here (Bilaspur volume: Nihang Bairagi)
quote: The village is held mokasa by the Mahant of Seorinarayan for the maintenance of a shrine there.

what: Chhattisgarh a headquarters of dissent; large part of population Kabirpanthi and Satnami (Satnami movement founded by Ghasi Das, Chamar)
quote: A' large proportion of the population belongs to the two great dissenting'sects of Kabirpanthis and Satnamis

what: Kabirpanthi fair for Ghasi Das on Magh Paurnima, ~5,000 attendance, 15 days; samadhi visited by representative of the Kawardha Mahant
quote: There is a samadhi (tomb) of the Kabirpanthi Gurti Ghasi Das which is visited periodically by a representative of the Mahant at Kawardha

what: Rajim fair named as the greatest fair of the district (Rajiva Lochan temple, Vaishnava); no mahant or ascetic order named in the Raipur text
quote: The fair ranks next in importance to the great Rajim fair
